data.title: American Express reaffirms 10% revenue growth and raises 2026 EPS outlook to $18.30-$18.60 amid restructuring
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: American Express (AXP) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We had another strong quarter with record revenues of $20 billion, up 9% and EPS of $5.42 reported and $4.68 on an adjusted basis." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • "Given our strong performance year-to-date, we are reaffirming our revenue growth guidance of 10% and raising our EPS guidance to between $18.30 and $18.60 on a reported basis or between $17.60 and $17.90 on an adjusted basis." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • "As a result, we took a $336 million charge for restructuring in the quarter, which is expected to result in the elimination of approximately 5% of our positions globally." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • "Yesterday's announcement of our exclusive partnership with Airbnb... we're excited to bring over 1 million listings globally into our Amex Travel program as well as expanding travel benefits for eligible U.S. card members." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • "Q3 was another strong quarter, and we continue to see good momentum across the business." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "We reported GAAP EPS of $5.42 this quarter, up 31%." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)

Outlook

  • "We are reaffirming our full year revenue growth guidance of 10% and raising EPS guidance to a range of $18.30 to $18.60 and $17.60 to $17.90 on an adjusted basis." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "The fine does not impact our full year 2026 guidance." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • "The orders do not impose an asset cap on the company and the costs associated with the remediation are not anticipated to affect 2027 guidance." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • Compared with Q2, management moved from "We continue to expect full year EPS of $17.30 to $17.90" (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri, Q2) to the higher Q3 EPS ranges above, while maintaining the 10% revenue growth target.

Financial Results

  • "Revenue was $20.1 billion, up 9% year-over-year." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "Net card fee growth accelerating to 17% FX adjusted." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "We acquired 3.1 million new cards in the quarter with 76% of new accounts on fee-paying products." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "Overall provision expense was $985 million, including a reserve release of $211 million." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "In Q3 specifically, we returned $2.2 billion of capital to shareholders, including $1.6 billion of share repurchase and $0.6 billion of dividends." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)
  • "We ended the quarter with a CET1 ratio of 10.9%, reflecting the gain from the sale of GBTG that happened at the end of the quarter." (Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec)

Q&A

  • Sanjay Sakhrani, Keefe, Bruyette, & Woods, Inc.: asked about rewards "gamify" risk; Chairman & CEO Squeri responded, "we really don't have a breakage model" and added, "we have levers within our model... we can get to spend thresholds that require those benefits to be made."
  • Ryan Nash, Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.: asked about sustaining spend and mid-teens EPS into 2027; CFO Le Caillec said, "we're not going to get into guidance for 2027" but added VCE should "stabilize" and "help us just like maintain that mid-teens EPS ambition"; CEO Squeri highlighted, "Resy restaurants were up 18%" and "Fine Hotels and Resorts and The Hotel Collection, that's up 50%."
  • Donald Fandetti, Wells Fargo Securities, LLC: asked about premium competition/market share and international moderation; CEO Squeri said international was "22 straight quarters of double-digit growth rate" and added, "we continue to do well, and we're getting the share of revenue that we're looking to get."
  • L. Erika Penala, UBS Investment Bank: pressed on AI-enabled rewards maximization and financial impact; CEO Squeri said, "it's a little too early in the game to determine what the impact will be on VCE" and added Amex will take "a risk-based approach" and allow access only via "approved through API or MCP channels."
  • Bill Carcache, Piper Sandler & Co.: asked if premium competitive intensity feels different; CEO Squeri said, "we really don't see much different than what we've seen" and added the segment expansion has "introduced more people into that part of the TAM."
  • Robert Wildhack, Autonomous Research: asked about allowance coverage ratio; CFO Le Caillec pointed to conservative scenarios and said the 2.6% reserve rate reflects "the premiumization of the portfolio."
  • John Pancari, Evercore ISI: asked about card-fee growth trajectory; CFO Le Caillec said, "we saw that inflection point this quarter" and reiterated, "Again, you're going to have to wait until January for that" on 2027.
  • Terry Ma, Barclays Bank PLC: asked about revolve runway; CFO Le Caillec said borrowing penetration has been "stable" and emphasized, "we're not changing our underwriting approach here."
  • Darrin Peller, Wolfe Research: asked about commercial acceleration milestones; CEO Squeri said middle market is where Amex "have not grown the way we want to grow" and positioned Center plus "more agents" to compete with "Ramp and with Brex."
  • Mihir Bhatia, BofA Securities: asked about the Visa/Mastercard settlement and network strategy; CEO Squeri said, "we've really pivoted" away from "partner with the bigger banks" toward partners like "Synchrony" and "Bread Financial," and added on surcharging, "it doesn't really appear to have affected anybody's business."
  • Cristopher Kennedy, William Blair & Company: asked about banking products; CEO Squeri said, "I think you'll see this continue to play a bigger part in our overall strategy" and noted "the launch this quarter of the business savings account for our small business customers."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative to neutral, centered on potential pressure points (rewards gaming, competitive intensity, reserve conservatism, interchange/surcharging), including explicit framing like "concerns" about rewards being "gamify" (Sakhrani, KBW) and requests for quantification of "financial impact" from rewards maxing (Penala, UBS).
  • Management: slightly positive in prepared remarks and mostly neutral in Q&A; confidence language included "We are on track to deliver another year of 10% revenue growth and mid-teens EPS growth" (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri), while uncertainty language appeared on open questions like rewards-maxing economics: "it's a little too early in the game" (Chairman & CEO Squeri).
  • Versus Q2, management tone added more defensiveness/compliance emphasis tied to the OCC action ("we are accountable for addressing them thoroughly" (Chairman & CEO Squeri)), while Q2 emphasized reinvestment choice-making ("We've chosen" to invest rather than drop to bottom line (Chairman & CEO Squeri, Q2)).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance shifted from Q2: "We continue to expect full year EPS of $17.30 to $17.90" (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri, Q2) to Q3: "raising our EPS guidance to between $18.30 and $18.60" (Chairman & CEO Squeri), while keeping 10% revenue growth guidance in place.
  • Strategic emphasis broadened from Q2 premium value propositions and partnerships (including TheFork discussion) to Q3’s heavier focus on AI and "Agentic Commerce" plus new travel distribution via Airbnb.
  • Q3 introduced discrete items absent from Q2’s headline framing, including the GBTG transaction gain usage and a restructuring program: "a $336 million charge" and "approximately 5%" headcount reduction (Chairman & CEO Squeri).
  • Analyst focus moved from Q2 sustainability of elevated U.S. consumer spend and reinvestment pacing to Q3’s concentration on AI-driven rewards optimization, competitive pressure in premium, and reserve/CECL framing.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Adjusted EPS includes an expense for legal matters, which includes the unreserved portion of the recently announced civil money penalty levied by the OCC." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • "The deficiencies cited in the consent orders should not have occurred, and we are accountable for addressing them thoroughly." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)
  • Management flagged execution and control needs around AI access: "We're just not going to let assistants run rogue through our systems." (Chairman & CEO Stephen Squeri)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a record-revenue quarter while reaffirming 10% full-year revenue growth and lifting 2026 EPS guidance, alongside disclosing a $336 million restructuring charge tied to an expected ~5% global workforce reduction. Leadership highlighted the Airbnb partnership and a broadened AI strategy spanning acquisition, engagement, payments, and servicing, while stating that the OCC penalty and related remediation are not expected to change 2026 guidance and are not anticipated to affect 2027 guidance.

data.title: Wells Fargo, Arm, Intuit among companies objecting to tokenizing stocks on OKXICE - report
data.description:
Wells Fargo (WFC), Arm (ARM), and Intuit (INTU) have joined a list of companies that are objecting to their shares being "tokenized" on OKXICE, Reuters reported, citing a regulatory document.

Total number of ⁠companies ​that have now objected is 22, the document reportedly said.

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) that filed with the SEC to launch a tokenized securities platform for the 24/7 trading of U.S. stocks.

More than 60 listed companies were to be made available. Their shares were set to become tokens that trade on the blockchain via a liquidity pool and offer the same benefits as equities, such as dividends and voting rights.

However, the JV had encountered objections from issuers, the report published on Friday noted.

data.title: Analysts weigh in on Moderna's big drop following cancer vaccine results
data.description:
Moderna (MRNA) closed Thursday down ~17% after phase 3 data was leaked on the company's personalized cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene, and the Street is offering theories on why.

That data showed that intismeran autogene plus Merck's (MRK) Keytruda (pembrolizumab) cut the risk of melanoma returning or death by 42% vs. Keytruda alone, meeting the primary endpoint. The risk of distant metastasis or death, the secondary endpoint, was reduced by 38% compared to Keytruda alone.

One analyst said that the data wasn't as robust as in phase 2. Another stated that the combination could become the standard of care. And a third questioned whether it would become a transformative oncology therapy.

RBC Capital Markets' Lucca Issi, who has a sector perform on shares, noted that phase 2 data for recurrent free survival and distance metastasis free survival were, respectively, 49% and 59%.

Although the phase 2 trial enrolled an earlier cancer stage population compared to phase 3, "Nonetheless, if you look at the [intent-to-treat population] (which is the way the FDA looks at it), the HRs are numerically inferior vs Phase II....Overall, this is not the first time that we have seen impressive Phase II being followed by a more muted benefit in Phase III, but we do believe that this can't be confidence boosting..."

Piper Sandler's Edward Tenthof, who rates Moderna at overweight, said that Thursday's selloff was due to concerns that the standard of care will be neoadjuvant Keytruda. It is important to note that Keytruda has yet to be approved in this setting for melanoma.

"We believe the INTerpath-001 trial appropriately compared againstcurrent SOC and that approval in adjuvant melanoma would be an advantageous label and lead to clinical uptake," he wrote.

Citi's Geoff Meacham provided 10 reasons why, following the data, he doesn't like Moderna's risk/reward. Among them are that positive results do not mean a transformative modality change in treatment, it does not establish an "effective cure," and Moderna's valuation requires more than just the trial results.

"We agree that intismeran looks approvable in adjuvant melanoma, but the bigger picture is that it adds tumor sequencing, manufacturing lead time, treatment coordination and high cost to an already approved and highly effective anti-PD-1 backbone," Meacham wrote.

data.title: Booz Allen outlines FY2027 revenue of $11.3B-$11.6B while raising adjusted EPS to $6.50-$6.70 amid Ultra integration
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) Q2 FY2027

Management View

  • CEO Horacio Rozanski said the quarter stayed aligned with management’s plan: "Booz Allen is on track with the expectations we set for this fiscal year. We delivered strong profitability and cash generation while continuing to invest for the future." (CEO & Chair Horacio Rozanski)
  • Rozanski framed demand as being driven by mission urgency, noting: "demand for advanced technology solutions and products remains strong" while "Artificial or now super intelligence, or SI for short, is powering more sophisticated cyber threats." (CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • On cyber productization, Rozanski highlighted Vellox and a specific product result: "In testing at scale, Guile reduced attack success rates by more than 95%, and it is currently in private beta with government and commercial customers." (CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • On Defense Tech, Rozanski emphasized integration plans following the Ultra acquisition: "Now as one company, we will integrate our technologies to address mission gaps faster and more effectively than each of us could do alone." (CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • COO Kristine Anderson described operating conditions by segment: "National security continued to grow, while civil remained in transition." (COO & President Kristine Anderson)
  • Anderson said contract mix is shifting toward outcomes-based work: "Within national security, our firm fixed price contract mix has increased by 3 percentage points year-to-date." (COO & President Anderson)
  • CFO Troy Lahr summarized execution priorities as including awards, profitability, and cash generation: "I'm pleased with our continued strong operational execution, including capturing strategic awards, delivering profitability above our expectations and generating robust free cash flow." (Executive VP & CFO Troy Lahr)

Outlook

  • Lahr updated FY2027 revenue guidance to "between $11.3 billion and $11.6 billion, implying growth of 1% to 3%." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Lahr said the company expects "mid-single-digit growth for the full year" in national security, while Civil is expected to show "a low-double-digit decline for the year, slightly softer than our initial expectations." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Lahr raised profitability and cash expectations, stating: "We're raising the bottom end of our prior adjusted EBITDA guidance" to "$1.26 billion to $1.29 billion," and "We're raising our expected adjusted EPS range meaningfully" to "$6.50 to $6.70"; free cash flow is now expected "between $850 million and $925 million." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s posture of "reaffirming our guidance for the year across all metrics" and waiting to "roll in Ultra" after closing, Q2 included Ultra in guidance and lifted the adjusted EBITDA floor, adjusted EPS range, and free cash flow range. (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)

Financial Results

  • Lahr reported Q2 revenue "declined 3.9% year-over-year to $2.8 billion" and said the change was "largely due to a 10.6% decrease in billable expenses year-over-year" while "revenue ex billable expenses... was down less than 1% versus the prior period." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Lahr reported profitability and cash metrics as: "Adjusted EBITDA was $313 million at a margin of 11.3%" and "Adjusted diluted earnings per share increased 18% year-over-year to $1.76"; he added free cash flow was "$263 million." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • On demand indicators, Lahr said: "We had solid bookings during the quarter with a book-to-bill of 1.5x" and "Total backlog at the end of the second quarter was nearly $41 billion" with "funded backlog... increasing 5% year-over-year to $5.7 billion." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • On capital deployment tied to Ultra, Lahr stated: "we deployed a total of $965 million" including "$729 million for the Ultra Mission Solutions acquisition" and ended with "$334 million of cash on hand and total liquidity of $1.8 billion." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)

Q&A

  • Tobey Sommer, Truist: asked about fixed price/OTAs and margin implications; CEO Rozanski said, "the move to outcomes-based is something we embrace" and added the mix of "fixed price or outcome-based" is projected "to continue to grow" alongside "productizing a lot of our IP." (CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • Gautam Khanna, TD Cowen: asked where funded backlog increased and bookings outlook; CFO Lahr said national security funded backlog "was up 10%" and CEO Rozanski said under a continuing resolution, near-term bookings are "a little harder to predict" due to procurements "shift[ing] to the right." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr; CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • Louie DiPalma, William Blair: asked Vellox adoption; CEO Rozanski said "it's still early" and added: "the promise of those products will play out much more strongly over the next couple of years than over the next couple of quarters." (CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • Louie DiPalma, William Blair: asked what scope is removed in Civil recompetes; COO Anderson said it is "how much funding they're actually giving to the same activities" and noted, "there are no significant recompetes remaining for the fiscal year." (COO & President Anderson)
  • John Godyn, Citi: asked if margins can move into a higher regime; CEO Rozanski said, "we expect profit to grow faster than revenue and therefore, margins to expand over the next couple of years," while CFO Lahr cautioned about "lower civil volumes" and "timing of investments" in the next few quarters. (CEO & Chair Rozanski; Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Sheila Kahyaoglu, Jefferies: asked what drives national security acceleration and Ultra contribution; COO Anderson pointed to demand for "battle management solutions" and "space domain awareness," and CFO Lahr said Ultra should have "margins well above the 20%." (COO & President Anderson; Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Matthew Akers, BNP Paribas: asked about headcount stabilization; COO Anderson said, "we added over 300 employees in national security this quarter" and also said the company "will be decoupling growth from headcount." (COO & President Anderson)
  • Scott Mikus, Melius: asked if the growth algorithm still applies and resilience vs. budget cycles; CFO Lahr said, "we are... migrating away from that" and called decoupling "a gradual journey." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Seth Seifman, JPMorgan: asked about orders bifurcation and how to dimensionalize cyber exposure; CFO Lahr said the business remains "bifurcated" with national security strength, and CEO Rozanski described cyber as "our most rapidly transforming business" moving toward "technology-first" offerings. (Executive VP & CFO Lahr; CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • Jonathan Siegmann, Stifel: asked about election-cycle budget dynamics and procurement reform support; CEO Rozanski said reform has "bipartisan" support and added, "we're focused on execution" and "incorporate a variety of scenarios in our guide." (CEO & Chair Rozanski)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, with repeated probing on Civil timing, visibility under continuing resolutions, margin breakout potential, and whether Ultra is material enough to move results, including questions like "how do you think bookings play out" and whether procurements keep "moving to the right." (Gautam Khanna, TD Cowen; Gavin Parsons, UBS)
  • Management tone was slightly positive, leaning confident on medium-term margin expansion and technology differentiation, using language such as "gives me great confidence" and "we expect profit to grow faster than revenue" while still flagging near-term uncertainty around the "continuing resolution" and award timing. (CEO & Chair Horacio Rozanski)
  • Versus the prior quarter’s "cautious optimism" around budget uncertainty and a plan to update guidance after Ultra closed, management in Q2 sounded more anchored to execution with guidance updates already reflecting Ultra and multiple upward revisions. (CEO & Chair Rozanski)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q2 incorporated Ultra into guidance and raised FY2027 adjusted EBITDA to "$1.26 billion to $1.29 billion," adjusted EPS to "$6.50 to $6.70," and free cash flow to "$850 million to $925 million"; Q1 said the company would "reaffirm" guidance and "include into our guidance in October" what happens with Ultra after closing. (Executive VP & CFO Troy Lahr; CEO & Chair Horacio Rozanski)
  • Q2 messaging sharpened the bifurcation narrative: COO Anderson said, "National security continued to grow, while civil remained in transition," and CFO Lahr said Civil decline was "slightly better than we guided to last quarter" while award timing remains difficult to predict. (COO & President Anderson; Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Analyst focus broadened from Q1’s emphasis on funded backlog improvement and contract-type reform into Q2’s deeper push on margin regimes, Civil scope reductions, Ultra integration economics, and the pace of cyber product adoption. (John Godyn, Citi; Louie DiPalma, William Blair)

Risks and Concerns

  • CEO Rozanski reiterated budget-process risk: "we are now in a continuing resolution" and said near-term dynamics are "something we're watching very closely," especially for how it affects funding and awards. (CEO & Chair Rozanski)
  • Management described ongoing Civil execution risk tied to procurement delays, with COO Anderson stating, "Some of the larger bids are just pushing to the right," and CFO Lahr noting DSO elevation expectations due to acquisitions: "we expect our DSO to remain elevated... due to the Defy acquisition." (COO & President Anderson; Executive VP & CFO Lahr)
  • Integration and investment pacing were positioned as margin variables, with CFO Lahr saying the updated adjusted EBITDA range "implies a step down in margins in the second half" due to seasonality and "timing of investment spending," plus "incremental costs and interest expense associated with the Ultra acquisition." (Executive VP & CFO Lahr)

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q2 as execution tracking to plan despite federal budget uncertainty, emphasizing accelerating cyber and Defense Tech productization (including Vellox and Guile testing results) and the Ultra acquisition as a catalyst for scaling mission-proven defense tech offerings. Guidance for FY2027 was updated to $11.3B-$11.6B in revenue and raised ranges for adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow, while management continued to flag Civil timing and continuing-resolution dynamics as the main near-term swing factors.

data.title: Infosys forecasts 1%-2% FY'27 growth as $2B mega deal is expected to add over 1% next year
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Infosys (INFY) Q2 FY2027

Management view

  • "Our revenue growth for Q2 was 1.5% year-on-year and 1.2% sequentially in constant currency terms." (CEO Salil Parekh)

  • "AI revenue was a standout at 10.5% of our revenue, growing at 29% sequentially." (CEO Parekh) He added, "Large deals were another standout at $5.2 billion for the quarter," including "2 mega deals," with "one of these mega deals...for over $2 billion...for a period of 7 years...net new" and "expected to contribute over 1% revenue growth in the coming financial year." (CEO Parekh)

  • "Based on our Q2 performance and revised outlook for rest of the year, our revenue growth guidance is 1% to 2% year-on-year in constant currency terms." (CEO Parekh) He also said, "Our operating margin guidance remains at 20% to 22% for the year." (CEO Parekh)

  • "Our current guidance -- our last guidance was 1.5% to 3%." (CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka) He attributed the revision to demand and pricing factors: "Our Q2 has been softer and our volume continues to remain softer," and "We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on productivity." (CFO Sanghrajka)

Outlook

  • "Our revenue growth guidance is 1% to 2% year-on-year in constant currency terms." (CEO Salil Parekh) "Our operating margin guidance remains at 20% to 22% for the year." (CEO Parekh)

  • Management described multiple drivers behind the narrowed and lowered band versus last quarter’s 1.5% to 3%: "some of the sectors, we see softness, retail, high-tech, where the discretionary is lower than what we are expecting" and "continued intensity on pricing." (CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka)

  • Deal timing was flagged as a limiter for FY’27 benefit despite headline TCV: "The net new is only going to ramp up from later part of Q4" and "in this year, there's going to be a very miniscule amount of benefit...but the next year...it will contribute over 1% in our revenue." (CFO Sanghrajka)

Financial results

  • "Operating margin was stable at 21%." (CEO Salil Parekh) "Free cash flow was strong at $922 million for the quarter." (CEO Parekh)

  • CFO explained the quarter’s margin bridge, including discrete items: "We had a 70 basis points of impact on post-sale customer support" and "a 20 bps coming from our acquisition," offset by "40 basis points coming from the currency" plus "20 basis points...from a higher calendar and working day" and "20 basis points from the Project Maximus." (CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka)

  • Management framed second-half margin pressures without changing the annual range: "As you look forward...we will have impact coming from compensation" and "We will see continued intensity on pricing." (CFO Sanghrajka)

Q&A

  • Meghna Sen, CNBC-TV18: Asked why guidance was narrowed and about AI mix, furloughs, and vulnerable sectors; CEO Parekh said, "AI is really an incredible performance for us" and highlighted growth across "agents," "legacy modernization," and "process AI," while adding, "we see some weakness on the retail...and...on the high-tech." CFO Sanghrajka said, "pricing pressure" and "volume continues to remain softer" were baked into guidance.

  • Mansee Dave, ET Now: Pressed on weaker demand and whether AI monetization offsets pricing pressure; CEO Parekh said, "almost all" large deals had "some component" of AI and "1 or 2" were "full business transformation driven by AI," while also stating the company is "extremely clear" it will only take contracts meeting "economic guidelines." CFO Sanghrajka explained fresher hiring planning and noted, "We are working at 85% utilization."

  • Chandra R Srikanth, Moneycontrol: Asked why guidance tightened despite healthy TCV and about AI-driven cyber risk; CEO Parekh linked guidance to "competitive intensity" and contract discipline, and said, "we have a strong cyber business" and "it's something that we are looking to scale up even more."

  • Haripriya Suresh, Reuters: Asked how realistic it is for AI revenue to be "half in the next 2 to 3 years" and about U.S. immigration changes; CEO Parekh said AI growth could be "sustained" but "there will be some volatility," and added, "we don't see a change" in U.S. cost dynamics due to a majority "local hires." CFO Sanghrajka cited "discretionary related ramp downs" in high-tech and retail.

  • Beena Parmar, The Economic Times: Questioned cyber preparedness, mega deal sectors, and duration of AI deflation; CEO Parekh said client budgets "will go up" but "not disproportionately," and said the company is focused on "where the growth is" rather than the reduction. CFO Sanghrajka reiterated the net-new mega deal ramps mainly next year.

  • Shilpa Phadnis, The Times of India: Asked about PERM-related attrition and AI squeezing margins; CEO Parekh said, "We don't see any real impact on the attrition" and emphasized discipline when client productivity asks exceed achievable benefits: "it doesn't fit our economic profile." On GCCs, CEO Parekh said, "GCCs is an incredible growth area" and the business is "growing quite nicely."

  • Poulomi Chatterjee, Financial Express: Asked about mid-market expansion and frontier engineer targets; CEO Parekh said the company has "always worked with organizations which are not only large" but the "predominant focus is large companies," and on FDEs said, "the 6,000 was over the multiple years."

  • Uma Kannan, Deccan Herald: Asked about an eMudhra breach and geography softness; CEO Parekh said, "I don't have any specific comments on it right now." CFO Sanghrajka said, "The U.S. has been softer" while "Europe and the rest of the market has been stronger," and CEO Parekh added the coding-tools participation number "is increasing."

  • Jas Bardia, Mint: Pressed on slowing growth and margin impact; CEO Parekh reiterated focus on AI as a "$300 billion addressable market" and said productivity impacts are "a finite process," while adding margin discipline means "we don't take every contract" and referenced "a very strong cash flow generation machine."

  • Sanjana B, The Hindu Businessline: Asked about North America softness, offshoring, and GCC reversals; CFO Sanghrajka tied softness to "lower discretionary spend" and said offshoring is "always towards India," while CEO Parekh said Infosys is in discussions where it can "help them" or "take them and transform them" regarding GCCs.

  • Rukmini Rao, Fortune India: Asked if AI growth is driving subcontractor costs and about AI margins; CFO Sanghrajka said subcontractors stayed "between 8% to 9% of the revenue" and not specifically AI-driven, while CEO Parekh said, "we first don't disclose the margin externally separately on the AI."

  • Pooja Patil, Businessworld: Asked whether AI revenue is incremental and about the INR 26 interim dividend; CEO Parekh said AI revenue is "not something which is replacing what we have" and cited AI-led modernization as "new work." CFO Sanghrajka said the policy is "85% of the free cash flow" returned over five years and "Last quarter's dividend was INR 25...increased...to INR 26 now."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analyst/media tone was slightly negative, repeatedly pressing on the guidance cut, pricing pressure, and whether AI deflation is structurally compressing growth (e.g., questions on "weakest in 7 years" guidance and whether AI is "reclassified or replaced").

  • Management tone was slightly positive on AI and deal wins but more guarded on demand, repeatedly emphasizing discipline and uncertainty, including "volume continues to remain softer" and "continued intensity on pricing." (CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka)

  • Versus the prior quarter, management’s language shifted from highlighting a one-time termination impact to more persistent headwinds ("pricing pressure" and sector softness), while keeping margin guidance unchanged.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • AI revenue mix increased quarter-over-quarter: Q1 reported "AI services revenue was 8.2% of overall revenue" (CEO Salil Parekh) versus Q2 "AI revenue...10.5% of our revenue." (CEO Parekh)

  • Large deals expanded: Q1 "Large deals were $3.6 billion" (CEO Parekh) versus Q2 "Large deals...at $5.2 billion" with "2 mega deals." (CEO Parekh)

  • Full-year constant-currency revenue growth guidance moved lower: Q1 guidance was "1.5% to 3%" (CEO Parekh) versus Q2 "1% to 2%." (CEO Parekh)

  • Leadership topic was prominent last quarter but absent this quarter: Q1 Chairman Nandan Nilekani announced, "his time is coming to an end on March 31, 2027" for CEO Salil Parekh and named "Ashish Dash" as "CEO Designate"; Q2 prepared remarks and Q&A did not revisit the transition.

Risks and concerns

  • "We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on productivity." (CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka)

  • Management cited sector and geography pockets of weakness: "some weakness on the retail" and "some weakness on the high-tech" (CEO Salil Parekh), and "The U.S. has been softer over the last few quarters." (CFO Sanghrajka)

  • Execution and timing risk on backlog conversion was flagged: "The net new is only going to ramp up from later part of Q4" with limited benefit in the current year. (CFO Sanghrajka)

Final takeaway

Infosys management emphasized that Q2 featured accelerating AI mix and higher large-deal bookings, including a $2B, 7-year net-new mega deal expected to add over 1% growth next year, while also citing softer volumes, pricing pressure, and weakness in retail and high-tech as key reasons for tightening FY’27 constant-currency growth guidance to 1%-2% and reiterating 20%-22% operating margin guidance despite expected second-half compensation and pricing headwinds.

data.title: Booz Allen slides on Q2 revenue miss, hurt by civil division
data.description:
Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH) fell 4.3% in Friday's trading after reporting better than expected FQ2 adjusted earnings, but revenue declined 3.9% Y/Y to $2.78B, slightly below Wall Street consensus estimates, as the company's civil division continues to face headwinds.

Booz Allen (BAH) also raised guidance for full-year adjusted earnings of $6.50-$6.70/share from its previous forecast of $6.00-$6.35/share while narrowing its revenue outlook to $11.3B-$11.6B compared to its previous view for $11.2B-$11.7B.

Q2 profit ticked up to $181M, or $1.50/share, from $175M, or $1.42/share, in the year-earlier quarter, while the decline in revenue partly reflects an 11% reduction in billable expenses, with revenue excluding those expenses down less than 1% and national security revenue rising less than 1%, or 6% excluding billable expenses.

Q2 revenue from the civil business fell 15% Y/Y, as government contracts have generally become smaller in size and scope while fewer new programs have started, and the company said it now expects segment revenue to come in flat to slightly down in Q3 and Q4, with Ultra Mission Solutions largely offsetting the softer civil outlook.

Booz Allen (BAH) has a significant backlog of funded work to execute in the national security business, and it has aggressively increased hiring to support that demand, CFO Troy Lahr said on the company's earnings conference call, according to The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: Institutional tech selling pressure mounts as Nasdaq slides 6% from its record high
data.description:
Jefferies’ equity trading desk has recorded unusually heavy and persistent client selling in the technology sector, according to a recent investor note. 

Over the past 10 trading days, the desk was a net seller of tech stocks by more than $1 billion on seven of those sessions. The firm’s accompanying chart of 20-day rolling net flows in tech, media, and telecom shows one of the steepest declines in recent years, underscoring the intensity of the recent de-risking.

The flows arrive as the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) trades roughly -6% below the record high it set earlier this month. The index peaked on October 6 before giving back gains amid ongoing questions about the pace and returns of artificial-intelligence-related capital spending. While broader equity markets have held up better, the concentration of selling pressure in tech has weighed on the Nasdaq, which carries a heavy weighting in the largest technology and semiconductor names.

Jefferies described the 20-day period as one of the more dramatic stretches of net selling it has observed in the sector in recent years. The data reflect activity routed through the firm’s desk rather than total market-wide flows, but the consistency of large daily net sales has drawn attention as a clear sign of institutional position reduction. Investors continue to weigh whether the selling marks a temporary positioning washout or the early stage of a more sustained reevaluation of high-momentum technology holdings.

Nasdaq ETFs: (QQQ), (QQQM), (SQQQ), (TQQQ), (QLD), and (QID).

Tech ETFs: (VGT), (XLK), (IYW), (FTEC), (IXN), and (RSPT).
